haiku-low.q1: When the connection comes back, when the app comes to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while the phone is online.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it. It compares the change's base version with the note's current version; a mismatch is a conflict.
haiku-low.q4: The first write to arrive wins: note N at version 4 with the first phone's text. The losing text is saved as a new conflict note N2.
haiku-low.q5: One upload: a single queue row with the latest folded body, keeping its original change id and base version.
haiku-low.q6: Each queue row has a change id created once. The server stores each handled change id with its result, so a retry gets that stored result and nothing is written again.
haiku-low.q7: On the phone, in the sync state as the download cursor (last applied log sequence number). It updates only in the same local transaction that applies a download page.
haiku-low.q8: The page transaction did not commit, so the cursor did not move. The next sync restarts from the old cursor and replays the page with the same result.
haiku-low.q9: The phone learns from the upload response, which reports a conflict, the current version and the conflict note id. It then downloads log entries after its cursor, and its copy of the note updates to the winning text.
haiku-low.q10: After the phone has stored the server's response for it, accepted or conflict, and removed it from the queue.
haiku-low.q11: The download updates only the stored server version. The displayed text keeps the user's unsent edit.
haiku-low.q12: It goes into a new queue row for that note and waits until the in-flight change is resolved. Only one change per note is in flight at a time.

sonnet.q1: The connection coming back, the app coming to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while the phone is online.
sonnet.q2: Upload first, then download. The sync loops over upload batches until the queue is empty, then loops over download pages until the server reports no more.
sonnet.q3: The server. It compares the change's base version with the note's current version on the server. If they differ, the change is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first write to reach the server wins. The note becomes version 4 with the winner's text and gets a log entry 101. The loser's text is saved as a new conflict note (N2, title plus "(conflict)", version 1) with log entry 102. Nothing is merged. The applied-changes record holds the accepted and conflict results.
sonnet.q5: One change. The edits fold into a single queue row that keeps its change id and base version and holds the latest full body. The phone sends that one row.
sonnet.q6: Each queue row has a change id. The server's applied-changes record stores the result for each handled change id. A retry with the same id gets the stored result back and nothing new is written.
sonnet.q7: In the phone's sync state, as the download cursor (the last applied log sequence number). It is updated only in the same local transaction that applies a download page.
sonnet.q8: The phone's transaction does not commit, so the cursor does not move. The retry starts from the old cursor. Replaying entries is safe because they carry full bodies and versions.
sonnet.q9: The upload response says the change is a conflict, with the current version and the conflict note id. The phone removes the row from its queue and downloads from its cursor. That brings in the winning log entry, which updates its copy of the note to the winning text, and the conflict note.
sonnet.q10: When the server accepts the change, or when the server returns a conflict result and the phone has stored it. The row is removed only after the phone handles the response.
sonnet.q11: If the note has a queue row, the download updates only the stored server version. The displayed text keeps the user's unsent edit. The row's base version stays as it was. The server judges the change when it is sent.
sonnet.q12: It goes into a new queue row for that note and waits, because only one change per note is in flight. If the earlier change is accepted, the waiting row's base becomes the version the server gave that change. If the earlier change conflicts, the waiting row keeps its old base and the server judges it.
